summary: Audited main and PR #814. PR #814 safely keeps auth entry routes available by default and gates waitlist redirects behind PRELAUNCH_AUTH_REDIRECTS, but an unresolved review correctly noted the E2E route-health suite still expected waitlist redirects by default. Applied a safe test-only alignment so anonymous public auth routes and private route guards validate the configured redirect mode.
actions_taken: Validated PR #814 is open, non-draft, mergeable, and changes next.config.ts to make prelaunch auth redirects opt-in through PRELAUNCH_AUTH_REDIRECTS=true.

Validated PR #814 head had CI, Security CI, Full Security Suite, CodeQL, Gitleaks, Semgrep, Dependency Review, P0 Progress, P0 Runtime Evidence and related gates passing before the test-only follow-up.
Validated /api/prelaunch remains bounded, rate-limited, no-store, consent-only, and does not expose public email delivery diagnostics.
Validated cron remains a single protected daily maintenance aggregator.
Validated billing checkout still enforces authentication, organization scope, RBAC, trusted mutation, distributed rate limit, step-up, Stripe metadata, audit logging, and no-store responses.
Patched tests/e2e/route-health.spec.ts to assert waitlist redirects only when PRELAUNCH_AUTH_REDIRECTS=true and otherwise assert anonymous protected routes redirect to localized login.
Recorded this audit action in the append-only agent log directory because rewriting the large central agent_log.json from a truncated connector response would risk corrupting prior audit history.
